versions.name: Wehinahpay Mountain Camp

features.note: Hands-on vehicle upkeep and repair, including oil changes and tire rotations.
Shower houses with private stalls, each holding a toilet, sink and full-size shower.
A thirty-foot tower where Scouts learn climbing, rappelling and belaying.

An aerial adventure park with a multi-level ropes course of seventeen high and low elements, presented by the camp as one of the finest high ropes courses at any Scouting America summer camp and visible above the valley from anywhere in camp.
Trail to First Class, teaching new Scouts camping, fire building, wood tools, knots, lashings, first aid and map and compass.
Rainbow trout fishing on Crystal Lake, with open fishing in the evening program.
An ecology area based at the lake lodge and yurt.
A week-long COPE track for older Scouts.
The Derek Brooks Pavilion houses the scoutcraft area.
A range and target activities area with its own ranges, opened for free shooting in the evening program.
A trades and technology area housed in the camp technology center.
Flux core, gas torch and arc welding machines.

versions.summary: High-mountain resident summer camp for Scouts BSA operated by Conquistador Council, set at 8,500 feet in southern New Mexico.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it.
